runs.name: Matched control — S2 MTP-assistant k5 @8192 (same decode length)

campaigns.notes: Matched-workload proof FIRST (boxed 768, apples-to-apples): DSpark b16 (1866.46 TPS / QPS 2.98) beats S2 MTP-assistant k5 (1798.22 TPS / QPS 2.87) by +3.8% — correcting an earlier mis-verdict. True-S2 DSpark run decoded ~2295 tok/req (8192 cap) at 2634.58 TPS / QPS 1.15 in 871s. NOTE: the archived '~2403' S2 baseline rows decode a SHORTER output (~1320-1338 tok/req), so they are NOT a valid comparator for TPS/QPS at the true 8192 decode. A matched S2-MTP control decoding the same ~2295 tok/req is now in flight; the clean 8192 delta lands when it completes.

campaigns.name: int4 Quality A/B — FP8-Marlin control vs int4-Humming candidate

runs.name: Candidate — S2 int4 W4A16 Humming (GSM8K + BBH quality)

campaigns.notes: Acceptance = candidate within noise of control (<1-2% abs / 1-2 sigma per benchmark on GSM8K + BBH). int4 W4A16 halves weight bytes/HBM. Note: with DSpark already crossing 2500, this gate answers the W4A16 headroom/quality question rather than being the sole path to 2500. Both arms running in parallel (split to avoid the R51 shared-node reload wedge).
